rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial verb for forcibly taking money or property from a person or place.

example.english: They did rob a convenience store yesterday and even injured a clerk.
example.traditional: 佢哋噚日打劫咗間便利店，仲整傷咗個店員。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 cam4 jat6 daa2 gip3 zo2 gaan1 bin6 lei6 dim3 zung6 zing2 soeng1 zo2 go3 dim3 jyun4

rows.note: Use this specifically when someone enters a building to steal rather than confronting a victim.

example.english: Someone broke into the house to rob it last night.
example.jyutping: cam4 maan5 jau5 jan4 jap6 uk1 tau1 je5

rows.traditional: 搞到 A 冇晒 B
rows.jyutping: gaau2 dou3 A mou5 saai3 B
rows.note: Use this everyday construction when a situation leaves someone without a resource such as energy or time.

example.english: This assignment is enough to rob me of all my time.
example.traditional: 呢份功課搞到我冇晒時間。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 gung1 fo3 gaau2 dou3 ngo5 mou5 saai3 si4 gaan3
